A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same QVGen work, with matching core algorithms, model families and experiments. All 28 pages of v3 and 34 pages of v5, including appendices, support comparison through text extraction and visual inspection. Relocated and renumbered material can be matched.

before.justification: v3 reports original video-generation benchmarks, image-generation results, gradient analyses, ablations, generated samples and computational measurements in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v5 retains those original empirical results and adds fine-tuning controls, further ablations, a SVDQuant combination, training-cost comparisons and operator-level profiling.

M1.justification: The core auxiliary-module and iterative SVD/rank-decay procedure in Section 3 and Algorithm 1 is unchanged. However, v5 Appendix I introduces a hybrid procedure that initializes QVGen from SVDQuant's modified weights, quantization parameters and low-rank factors, plus a variant that freezes model weights. These are localized procedural adaptations.

E1.justification: Both versions use OpenVidHQ-4M training videos, VBench and VBench-2.0 evaluation, and the existing image experiments involving LAION-5B, MJHQ-30K and GenEval. The four video models and SD3-medium are retained. The added studies vary optimization, quantization configurations or profiling procedures within existing task coverage.

E2.justification: v5 adds Full Fine-tuning controls for both models in Table 1 and Linear, Sparse with Wanda, and Sparse with MaskLLM alternatives in Table 6. The retained SD3-medium comparison also adds LSQ and EfficientDM alongside Q-DM in Appendix Table Q, corresponding to v3 Table T. These materially broaden comparator membership in existing experiments.

E3.justification: The established training-data, epoch and benchmark-sampling protocols remain unchanged. New evaluation designs include same-data full-precision fine-tuning, gradient-clipping thresholds of 1.0/0.5/0.1, decay durations of 0.75/1/1.5 epochs, weight-only versus activation-only quantization, and operator-level A800 latency/throughput profiling. These substantially expand experimental controls and measurement procedures without establishing that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v5 adds tests of whether clipping alone helps QAT, sensitivity to zero/random initialization, decay-phase duration, and the relative difficulty of weight and activation quantization. It also tests weight freezing in the SVDQuant hybrid, strengthens decay-strategy ablations, expands training-loss comparisons, and analyzes computational bottlenecks. These address several substantive mechanism and robustness questions beyond v3's existing ablations.

E5.justification: The randomized-decay experiment already reports three trials and standard deviations in v3 Table S; v5 Table O retains the same practice and values. The fixed-seed qualitative comparison is also retained. No new repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty-estimation procedures are reported.

E6.justification: Existing headline benchmark entries and qualitative samples are retained, but v5 adds substantial results for controls, ablations, hybrid quantization and efficiency. For example, Table F newly reports hybrid Aesthetic Quality 56.23 and Scene Consistency 17.65; Table Q adds LSQ/EfficientDM FIDs of 14.87/15.23; Table R reports measured INT4 throughput of 345–872 TOPS. These are additional results, not cross-version gains for unchanged configurations.

T1.justification: The original convex regret theorem and proof are retained, moving from Appendix C to B. v5 adds Appendix C with smoothness, bounded learning-rate and lower-bounded-objective assumptions, a nonconvex stationarity theorem, and its proof. It derives an O(1/T) bound on average squared gradient norm for exact gradient descent, substantially extending the formal analysis.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same principal contributions: video-generation QAT, auxiliary modules motivated by gradient norms, rank decay without additional inference overhead, effective 3/4-bit quantization, and claimed full-precision-comparable 4-bit quality. The headline improvements of 25.28 in Dynamic Degree and 8.43 in Scene Consistency remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v5 adds the hypothesis that model weights progressively absorb quantization errors, explanations for over-clipping and random-initialization failures, and an interpretation of the hybrid experiment supporting weight updates. It also discusses slower decay, activation-quantization difficulty, and attention/quantization overhead as practical speed limits. These substantially expand mechanism explanations and applicability qualifications; the existing cross-domain limitations remain.

D1.justification: v5 newly announces code/model repository access and discloses the default clipping threshold of 1.0 and LSQ's non-distillation objective. It documents Wanda's 128-sample pruning setup, learned MaskLLM masks, hybrid initialization, and NVTX profiling with explicit operator shapes and stage timings. These materially expand reproducibility information; the newly disclosed settings do not establish changes to earlier runs.

R1.justification: v5 adds optimization references for nonconvex analysis, Wanda and MaskLLM references, and citations including LinVideo, Harmonica and Nagel's quantization overview. The principal positioning relative to prior video quantization remains intact. Most video-diffusion related work is moved from v3 Appendix A into Section 5 rather than newly introduced.

P1.justification: Most abstract, introduction and method prose remains intact. v5 makes local wording edits, separates training and inference efficiency discussion, moves video-diffusion related work into the main text, and reorganizes appendices around added analyses. Affiliations and publication headers are updated, with acknowledgements and an LLM-writing-assistance disclosure added. This is a limited restructuring rather than an extensive rewrite.

P2.justification: v5 adds a multi-method training-loss figure, a weight-versus-activation quantization montage, and several training-cost, ablation and profiling tables. Existing comparison and initialization tables gain rows. Together these substantially expand the visual presentation. The earlier qualitative samples are retained and repaginated as Figures C–J, rather than replaced with new samples.

improvement.justification: The added fine-tuning and stronger decay controls, initialization/clipping tests, and measured runtime breakdowns improve support for the method and clarify practical tradeoffs beyond v3's existing analyses. Code/model access information and implementation disclosures improve reproducibility documentation. The theoretical gain is limited: the new nonconvex proof concerns smooth exact-gradient descent and does not establish convergence of the reported STE/AdamW procedure or resolve the causal gradient-norm interpretation.
